title: Extension bundles install without signature verification
description:
ExtensionInstaller.swift:46-64 installs any .crx/.xpi/.zip by stripping the CRX header (ExtensionArchive.swift:67) and writing the ZIP to disk; the CRX2/CRX3 signature is never validated and unsigned .xpi/.zip install with no provenance. Anyone who opens a malicious bundle runs its code with full extension privileges. WebKit provides no signing store, so the browser must check.

DECISION (2026-08-07): trust model is WARN-BUT-INSTALL. Unknown or missing signer is not blocked; the UI shows an unverified-developer warning before the bundle is enabled. Verified signatures from a pinned key are trusted silently. No paid Apple signing identity required.
design: Verify CRX2/CRX3 signatures against a pinned public key (store key or developer key); unknown/missing signer is allowed but flagged in the UI before enable. .xpi/.zip carry no signature, so they always take the warn path. Reuse ExtensionArchive byte parsing; keep bundle load path unchanged. Surface verification result (verified / unverified) on the extension row and in an install-time confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: CRX2/CRX3 signatures are actually verified against a pinned public key (not stripped-and-ignored); unsigned .xpi/.zip and unknown-signer bundles still install but the UI shows an unverified-developer warning at install and on the extension row, and they are not silently trusted; tampered bundles are detected and flagged; tests cover tampered, unsigned, valid, and unknown-signer bundles
close_reason: CRX2/CRX3 signatures verified at install in new BrowserCrypto package; warn-but-install UI (row icon, install message, enable confirmation); verdict persisted as <slug>.verification; 10 verifier + 4 installer + 3 UI tests; prepush green

title: Extension worker recovery: Bitwarden login needs a live worker port
description:
After the popup fix (f247903), Bitwarden's UI opens and renders. Logging in fails:

- 'Failed to unlock via master password' on a correct password. The stack lands on a null assertion (Gp), not a hash compare; next to it:
  'Invalid call to runtime.connect(). No runtime.onConnect listeners found.'
  'Invalid call to port.postMessage(). The port is disconnected.'
  So the popup's secure-messaging port never connects to the worker and Bitwarden reports it as a wrong password.
- After the email verification code, the flow spins forever; same port, plus
  'Unchecked runtime.lastError: Invalid call to tabs.create(). It is not implemented.'

WebKit does not queue runtime.connect until the worker registers onConnect (Chrome does) and does not restart a crashed MV3 worker. The reference browser solves this with a dedicated subsystem not yet ported:
- Sources/Search/ExtensionWorkerRecovery.swift (187 lines): watches WebKit's private _backgroundWebView, generation numbers, register/created/unregister, observe/cancel through native messaging and a webkit.messageHandlers bridge for content worlds.
- Sources/Search/ExtensionShims.swift lines ~1180-1300: worker generation stamping, passive port tracking with WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry, rewake on connect, keepalive.

Attempts so far: calling context.loadBackgroundContent before showing the popup made the popup paint blank; a shim-side connect-retry proxy was written but not verified and was reverted to keep f247903's working popup. main is clean at f247903.

Acceptance: with Bitwarden installed fresh, unlock succeeds with the correct master password, email-code login completes, and no 'No runtime.onConnect listeners found' appears in chord.log. Also implement chrome.tabs.create natively if the 2FA flow needs it.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-26 (worker recovery, phase 1).

Landed:
- ExtensionWorkerRecovery (ChordExtensions): per (Space, slug) generation + background lifetime; observes WebKit's private _backgroundWebView and the @objc didCreateBackgroundWebView delegate callback; registers before controller.load; unregisters/raises the generation on unload/reload; content-script bridge (chordWorkerRecovery, world WebExtension-<slug>, registered on every engine user content controller).
- Router: background.observe / background.unobserve (long-held reply, no 15s shim timeout).
- Shim: wraps runtime.connect + runtime.onConnect; tracks ports; on a new generation synthesizes onDisconnect (Chrome semantics) so the extension reconnects; keepalive on port traffic. Worker block is inert without a manifest background.
- Host: revive on WKWebExtensionContextErrorDomain backgroundContentFailedToLoad (same-context unload+load, max once/60s).
- Tests: 4 state-machine tests, 4 shim-worker JS tests, 3 router tests (212 ChordExtensions tests green). prepush green.

NOT yet verified: Bitwarden unlock + email-code flow on a real install (needs the app + extension; not possible from the CLI test run). Manual acceptance from the issue description still stands. tabs.create already landed in 4da9b0f.
FOLLOW-UP (same day): load now re-runs ExtensionShimInstaller.prepare when the sidecar fingerprint is stale, off the main actor, before WKWebExtension reads the bundle — so extensions installed before this build get the worker-recovery shim without a reinstall. Test: loadingAnUnpreparedBundleShimsItBeforeWebKitReadsIt (real offscreen round trip) + loadingAnInstalledExtensionBringsAnOldShimUpToDate. 213 ChordExtensions tests; prepush green.
2026-10-27: native half ported into main (from backup 71c25b8 / Search). ExtensionWorkerRecovery, per-(Space,slug) generations, private background-created delegate, background.observe/unobserve wiring, content-script chordWorkerRecovery bridge through ExtensionControllerHandle, reload/unload/revive lifecycle. Live temp-world Bitwarden popup now renders its onboarding screen (no spinner, no 'No runtime.onConnect' log). Login/unlock acceptance still needs a real account; issue stays open for that.
close_reason: Worker/port recovery ported and verified live: Bitwarden unlock with master password, autofill on Google sign-in, no runtime.onConnect/port errors. Passkeys remain blocked on the missing web-browser public-key-credential entitlement (40q).

title: Extension popup opens only once: use a Chord-owned popover like the reference
description:
User report: clicking the Bitwarden toolbar icon sometimes does nothing.

Reproduced in ChordTest with logs: the click reaches 'presentAction', WebKit reports action.presentsPopup=true and action.popupPopover != nil, but the presentation delegate is never called again after the first show. Instrumentation removed; commit 3debdf7 is the last state.

The reference browser does not use WebKit's popover at all:
  let url = action.popupWebView?.url ?? popupURL(for: context)
  action.closePopup()
  ExtensionPopup.shared.show(url, for: context, from: anchor(for: context.uniqueIdentifier))

It closes WebKit's popup, takes its URL, and presents its own NSPopover with a fresh WKWebView, so a second click is an ordinary new popover. Chord currently reuses action.popupPopover (WebKitExtensionHost.presentActionPopup), which appears to be single-shot.

Fix: port that shape — own popover (size to content, transient, Escape closes, anchor beside the extension button, per-Space), close WebKit's popup first, and keep the extension context so popup pages can use chrome.runtime. Add an XCUITest that opens the popup twice in a row (install a fixture extension with a popup; the store install stays manual).
close_reason: Fixed. Extension popups are Chord's own hidden-titlebar panel, opened from the manifest URL without calling performAction or didOpenTab; controller now gets an app-supplied webViewConfiguration; shim defines Symbol.dispose/asyncDispose. Verified with Bitwarden: opens on every press, renders the unlock screen, takes typed input, and Unlock returns 'Invalid master password' for a wrong one. prepush green.

title: Extension install: unpack CRX payload to a folder (foundation)
description:
Change the install pipeline so an extension is a folder, not a zip. ExtensionInstaller currently keeps the ZIP and hands it to WKWebExtension(resourceBaseURL:) (ExtensionInstaller.swift:76, WebKitExtensionHost.swift:174). Unpack the verified payload into <slug>/, keep the <slug>.verification sidecar, load the folder, and migrate existing zip installs on launch.

This is the prerequisite for shims, CWS install and chrome-extension:// serving.
design: Keep the ExtensionHost boundary (ADR 011). Verification happens before unpacking; after unpacking, the folder is ours to modify (shims) but the sidecar records the verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh install, reinstall and migration of an existing zip install all produce a folder that loads; the verification sidecar still reflects the original bytes; uninstall removes the folder; tests cover a CRX3, a plain ZIP and a tampered bundle.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Chrome API shims: native messaging channel + chrome.offscreen
description:
Inject a shim script into an installed extension (background worker, module worker import, every content script) and add the nativeMessaging permission it needs. The shim defines the Chrome APIs WebKit lacks and forwards calls as native messages to Chord, which answers natively.

Subset for this task: chrome.offscreen (createDocument/closeDocument with reason + justification, real hidden web view), chrome.storage.session, chrome.privacy (read-only current values). Not the full Search surface.

Search reference: Sources/Search/ExtensionShims.swift (302 KB) and ExtensionOffscreen.swift (14 KB) — read the offscreen part only; do not port the file.
design: ChordExtensions: prep step after unpack, message router, hidden WKWebView lifecycle. Permission added by us must be recorded so the UI shows what the extension asked for, not what we added. Depends on the folder install task.
acceptance_criteria: A real MV3 password manager (Bitwarden) installs, starts its worker, unlocks and autofills in a Space; an extension without offscreen behaves exactly as today; shim injection is idempotent and re-applied when the extension is reinstalled; no extension can spoof another's id; failures surface an error list per extension.
notes: Probe result (899.2): chrome.offscreen absent everywhere; WebKit silently drops the 'offscreen' permission and createDocument throws. Shim must define chrome.offscreen in JS and answer via nativeMessaging. chrome.storage.session ALREADY EXISTS in the SW, so do not shim it; only add setAccessLevel(TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS) when content scripts need it. chrome.scripting exists but enumerates zero own properties -> detect with typeof, never Object.keys.

title: Tab discard/sleep (keep tab, free the web view)
description:
Distinguish sleeping from archiving. A slept tab keeps its sidebar row, title, favicon, history and scroll position but has no live WKWebView/process. Wake on selection.

Reuse what exists: WebEngine.snapshot already 'captures interactionState, tears the view down' (WebEngine.swift:468) and interactionState restore already backs session restore. Add Tab.isSleeping + a timer (idle 30 min, then 2 h) and exempt: active tab, pinned/favourite, playing audio, form with typed text, ongoing download, split pane partner, private tabs.

Search reference: Sources/Search/Sleep.swift (9 KB) plus Closing.swift for the auto-close policy we already approximate.
design: Store: isSleeping flag + timers. Engine: call existing snapshot/teardown path, no new WebKit API. UI: sleeping styling in the sidebar row. Must not fight the ephemeral sweep timer.
acceptance_criteria: Measured memory drop with N tabs slept (before/after footprint); waking restores scroll, form text and back/forward history; a slept tab never appears as blank; exemptions unit-tested; archive and sweep behaviour unchanged.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: [epic] Port selected reference-browser features into Chord
description:
Source: https://github.com/driceroland/Search (MIT, Swift/AppKit+SwiftUI+WKWebView, ~42k lines, one file per concern). Cloned at /Users/rizal/perkodingan/Search for reference. Feature-by-feature diff against Chord done 2026-10-25.

Contradicts two claims in our docs: (a) 'No passkeys. Not possible.' — Search carries the WebAuthn ceremony via ASAuthorizationWebBrowserPublicKeyCredentialManager + com.apple.developer.web-browser.public-key-credential (Apple grants on request; needs Developer ID provisioning profile). Already tracked as 40q. (b) 'MV3 password managers die on chrome.offscreen' — Search implements chrome.offscreen natively via a shim, so the class is not unfixable.

PHASE 1 — quick wins, no architecture change (~1 week, each independent):
- Copy Clean Link: strip utm_*/fbclid etc., keep unknown params + fragment, leave signed URLs alone. Replace existing Copy URL action.
- Tab discard/sleep: timer + reuse WebEngine.snapshot (already 'captures interactionState, tears the view down', WebEngine.swift:468) + isSleeping flag; keep tab, scroll, history. Distinct from archive/close.
- Media-key release: silence MPNowPlayingInfoCenter when media idle so Now Playing returns to other apps.
- Keyword shortcuts: 'yt cats' -> %s template, http(s) only.
- Address-at-rest: active tab shows registrable domain instead of title; flag punycode; needs eTLD+1 list.
- Settings search (find-a-setting), What's New card, AppleScript sdef (read-only tabs/URL/title), blocked-popup tray with per-site allow.
- Import: bookmarks HTML (Netscape) first; Arc StorableSidebar.json -> Spaces/pins second.

PHASE 2 — real features, no API risk:
- Reader mode (DOM prose heuristic, isolated world, reuse panel chrome).
- Site-search chips (prefix -> 'Search Reddit', OpenSearch discovery).
- Chromium password import (GRDB reads Login Data; decrypt with 'Safe Storage' keychain key).

PHASE 3 — extension layer (the one structural change; everything extension-related hangs on it):
- Unpack extension ZIP to a folder at install, inject shim.js into background worker + content scripts, add nativeMessaging permission, load folder via WKWebExtension(resourceBaseURL:). ExtensionInstaller currently keeps the ZIP and hands it to WebKit directly (ExtensionInstaller.swift:76).
- Shim subset only: chrome.offscreen, storage.session, privacy, minimal userScripts. Answer via native messaging. Unblocks Bitwarden/1Password class.
- Then, separately: Chrome Web Store install (port Crx.swift: CWS update endpoint + CRX3 id/signature check), native messaging hosts (unsandboxed app, so Process launch is fine), chrome-extension:// scheme instead of webkit-extension://.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (evaluated, rejected):
- Passkeys: blocked on Apple-granted entitlement + Developer ID profile (see 40q).
- Apple Passwords / iCloud Keychain bridge: reverse-engineered OS protocol, breaks silently on macOS updates.
- Profiles: requires reworking TabStore/data root/keychain naming/per-Space extension controllers — multi-week persistence refactor.
- AI suite: Search ships it disabled (AI.shipped = false); needs signed helper process + hosted model; product decision.
- Floating video: we already have native PiP.
- Bench automation socket: port only open/wait/text/click/shot subset if E2E flakiness becomes real.
- Content blocking, YouTube ad skipping, Spaces: ours is stronger; keep.

METHOD: do NOT copy-paste — Search has no layered boundaries (one file per concern, everything imports WebKit). Extension work must stay behind ExtensionHost in ChordExtensions per ADR 011; budget +50% for extension items, +0% for UI/JS items.
design: Touchpoints: Engine (WebEngine.snapshot, page scripts, isolated world), Extensions (ExtensionInstaller ZIP->folder, shim injection, native messaging channel), Store (settings keys, tab isSleeping flag), UI (menus, settings sections), ChordCrypto (CRX3 verify, already present). No new third-party dependency; PSL list vendored or system.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1 features ship behind existing menus/settings with tests; tab discard measurable as memory drop with tab + scroll + history intact; extension shim subset loads a real MV3 password manager (Bitwarden) end-to-end in a Space; docs updated (README, USER_GUIDE, BROWSER_SPEC, CHECKPOINT) and ./scripts/prepush.sh green.
notes: 2026-10-25: all 21 children merged to main and closed. prepush.sh green (branding gate + packages + tests + app). ChordTest.app isolation verified: own data root, WebKit store, preferences and vault service; real Chord data mtimes unchanged after launch. Local fixture site prepared at /tmp/chord-test/site (article, link farm, login, translate, popups, late content). Remaining: GUI smoke pass with cliclick/screenshots — blocked while the screen is locked; external AppleScript check needs one Automation approval. Decisions pending: keep 21 merge commits vs squash, per repo's linear-history note.
close_reason: All 21 ported features merged and verified. UI smoke suite added (9 XCUITest cases, isolated app copy). Full prepush green, branding gate green. Manual evidence: reader, keywords, site chips, popup tray path; UI suite covers hover, row menu, settings search, blocked popups.

title: Extension user-gesture propagation + exception reporting (Safari 27)
description:
Safari 27 WebKit web-extension runtime now: (1) propagates user gestures through sendMessage/connect/postMessage/executeScript, so extensions can do media playback and other activation-requiring actions reliably; (2) reports uncaught JS exceptions + unhandled promise rejections in extension scripts; (3) adds runtime.getDocumentId().

Chord impact: per-Space WKWebExtensionController host (ADR 011). The gesture fix removes a whole class of 'extension action silently fails' bugs. The exception reporting feeds the ExtensionsPanel debugging story and directly addresses the 'popup spins forever / WKWebExtensionContextErrorDomain code 6' diagnosis pain in the chord-browser-maintenance skill.

Host is macOS 26.7 with Xcode 27 SDK (Safari 27 WebKit APIs run on macOS 26). One caveat: the new runtime surface (getDocumentId, exception reporting) should be probed at runtime on this build, since extension-runtime behavior can lag the WKWebView API.

Work: verify the new runtime surfaces on the macOS 27 SDK, surface extension-script errors in the extensions UI (ExtensionsPanel) / log, add getDocumentId-based debugging aid.

Acceptance: an extension calling media playback via sendMessage works with a user gesture; uncaught extension-script exceptions appear in AppLog/ExtensionsPanel; prepush green.
design: Gesture propagation is engine-side (mostly free). Our work: surface exceptions via the existing WKWebExtensionController host seams and AppLog; keep per-Space isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Media-playback extension works via sendMessage with gesture; extension-script exceptions visible in log; prepush green
notes: AVAILABILITY VERIFIED 2026-09-15: macOS 26.7 runtime WebKit (build 21624.5) does NOT implement the Safari 27 extension runtime surfaces. objc probe: willSubmitForm absent; WKContentWorld.worldWithConfiguration: absent; getCookiesForURL absent. Extension runtime changes are part of the same WebKit drop — expect none of them on macOS 26.7. Real gate is macOS 27 runtime. The extension-runtime probe caveat in the description stands and is now the whole story.

title: Native willSubmitForm hook for vault save/update prompts
description:
Safari 27 adds willSubmitForm callback on WKNavigationDelegate + WKFormInfo. Today password-vault form detection is a JS user script (PasswordFormMonitor, ChordEngine) that pierces shadow roots manually and can miss submits. Add a native delegate callback in the Engine that reports HTML form submissions, and route it into the existing vault save/update flow (WebEngine + TabStore). This replaces the fragile JS-driven submission path of ADR 016 and also covers cross-origin and shadow-DOM forms that the script misses.

Native APIs involved: WKNavigationDelegate.willSubmitForm(_:form:completionHandler:), WKFormInfo.

**Availability (verified 2026-09-15):** SDK 27 headers declare it, but macOS 26.7's runtime WebKit (build 21624.5) does NOT implement it — objc runtime probe returns false for the selector. Delegate method is safe to implement now (never fires on 26.7) but feature is dead code until macOS 27 runtime. Gate: . Do not expect it to work on this machine yet.

Acceptance: form submit on a test site triggers the vault save/update prompt even when the form lives inside a closed shadow root; existing PasswordFormMonitor tests stay green; prepush green.
design: RE-POINTED + IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24 on macOS 27.0 (26A428). The public WKNavigationDelegate.willSubmitForm (macOS 27, Beta) is declared but never invoked — verified with light-DOM, closed-shadow, and trusted-click probes. Working path: the SPI _WKInputDelegate._webView:willSubmitFormValues:frameInfo:sourceFrameInfo:userObject:requestURL:method:submissionHandler: (macOS 26.4+), set via the ObjC-runtime selector _setInputDelegate: (guarded by responds(to:)), the same SPI-by-selector approach already used for geolocation. It fires for a closed-shadow-root form and reports values + sourceFrameInfo + requestURL + method. Extraction by control name via ChordCore/NativeLoginCapture (shares LoginFormClassifier keywords); routed into the existing paneDidSubmitLogin flow. Kept additive: PasswordFormMonitor still covers fetch()-driven SPA logins; the store collapses duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Submit inside closed shadow root triggers vault save prompt; no regressions in vault fill tests; prepush green
notes: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-24 on macOS 27.0 (build 26A428): the public WKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:willSubmitForm:) is DECLARED (protocol_getMethodDescription present; Apple docs mark it Beta) but is NEVER INVOKED. Probes with a standalone WKWebView: a light-DOM GET form, a closed-shadow-root form, and a trusted CGEvent button click (form did navigate) all failed to fire it; only didStartProvisionalNavigation/didFinish fired. So the public API is still dead code on 27.0. WORKING PATH: the SPI _WKInputDelegate._webView:willSubmitFormValues:frameInfo:sourceFrameInfo:userObject:submissionHandler: has shipped since macOS 26.4 and reports values + frameInfo + sourceFrameInfo + requestURL + method. Implementing b0s should use that SPI (same 'call the SPI selector by name via the ObjC runtime' approach already used for geolocation), not the public Beta API. Reverted the public-API attempt; no code landed.
close_reason: Implemented via _WKInputDelegate SPI (macOS 26.4+). E2E: closed-shadow-root login triggers the vault save prompt; NativeLoginCaptureTests (9) + LoginCaptureE2ETests (6) green; prepush green.

title: P1: spike - Rust GTK4 shell + Swift core bridge (decision gate)
description: Prove the riskiest pieces before building the browser: (1) Rust workspace: gtk4 + libadwaita + webkit2gtk crates. (2) bindgen from chord_c.h; link Swift staticlib via cc crate. (3) Threading bridge: core on its own actor thread, events -> cross-thread channel -> g_idle_add -> GTK main loop. (4) Minimal window: sidebar (Spaces) + tab strip + one WebKitWebView; load URL, title/URL/progress round-trip through the core. (5) Session persistence round-trip (GRDB) on Linux. GATE: if the Swift staticlib+bindgen build chain or the threading bridge cannot be made solid, the whole approach is reconsidered.
acceptance_criteria: A Rust GTK4 window links the Swift core over C ABI, loads a URL in WebKitGTK, and round-trips title/URL/progress + session state through ChordCore/ChordStore running on Linux.

title: P0: carve the portable seam + C ABI (Linux-ready core)
description: No behaviour change; macOS stays green. (1) Neutralize WebEngine: strip WebKit shapes (WKWebsiteDataStore, AnyWebSurface, NSPrint, PiP) into capability protocols; WebKitEngine moves to ChordEngineApple. (2) New ChordPlatform protocols: SecretStore, AppLog, Geo, Notifier, Shortcuts, Updater, Clipboard. (3) ChordSecrets/ChordCrypto protocol + platform impls (macOS keeps Security/CryptoKit). (4) ChordLogging: drop os import -> sink protocol. (5) ChordStore: imports become protocols only (Foundation/GRDB + ChordPlatform). (6) C ABI module: chord_c.h + opaque chord_session_t* + callback registry (session/space/tab CRUD, nav, state, restore). (7) Linux CI: swift build + run Core/Persistence/Store tests on Ubuntu. (8) Verify prepush still green.
acceptance_criteria: ChordCore/ChordPersistence/ChordStore + C ABI target compile and their tests pass on Ubuntu in CI; macOS app and existing tests unchanged.

title: Command bar: '?' prefix forces search
description: QoL #3. Typing '?golang.org' (or '? golang.org') in the command bar must ALWAYS search 'golang.org', never navigate. Kills the URL-vs-search misfire class (URLInput.resolve treats any single dot-token as a host, URLInput.swift:55). Pure ChordCore change: URLInput.forcedSearchQuery helper + first branch in CommandBarRanking.fallback, so the search path never enters resolve's navigate branch. Spec: docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
